name: agent-plan
title: Agent Plan
description: An agent's plan laid out for agreement before anything runs — the user can reorder steps, remove one, or add their own, then run the plan as edited. The same component follows the run: give each step a `status` (`pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `done`, `failed`, `skipped`) and an optional `note`, and editing gives way to progress — the running step is marked and moves, a step waiting on the user holds still in the waiting colour, finished steps get a check, a failed step offers `onRetryStep`, `runStatus` names what's happening now, and `onStop` stays visible for the whole run. Takes `steps` (each with a `title`, optional `detail`, and an optional `needsApproval` flag for steps with external effects), an optional `title`, `onRun`, which receives the final ordered steps, an optional `onCancel`, and `allowAdd` to permit user-added steps. Steps that will stop for approval are labelled 'Asks for approval', and the header counts them, so the user knows before running where the agent will pause. Removing a step never deletes it outright: it stays in place struck through with an Undo, because a plan edit that cannot be seen or reversed is exactly the silent change the system exists to prevent. Reordering uses explicit move-up and move-down controls rather than drag, so it works identically by keyboard, touch and pointer, and every edit is announced through a live region. The run button reads 'Run edited plan' once anything changed. Plans are where an agent's misunderstanding becomes visible while it is still free to fix — once execution starts, a wrong step costs a tool call, a side effect, or a cancel and restart. This component is the agreement; execution belongs to Task Plan Runner. Composes AI Action Toolbar. Holds still, since it is the user's turn. Use it before multi-step runs, especially ones that touch external systems. Not for showing progress through a running plan.

meta.engineeringNotes: Separates agreeing on a plan from executing it, because the two need opposite designs: agreement is a still, editable surface where the user is in control, while execution is a moving status surface where the machine is. Merging them produces the common pattern where a plan is shown only as it starts running, which is too late to change it cheaply. Removal is modelled as a reversible state rather than a deletion — the step remains in place, struck through, numbered out of the sequence, with Undo — so an edit is always visible and never destructive. Reordering deliberately uses explicit up and down buttons instead of drag and drop: drag is pointer-first, hard to make accessible, and ambiguous on touch, while buttons behave identically across every input method and announce the resulting position through a live region (counting only steps that remain). The icon buttons are 32 pixels with hit areas extended vertically to 44, not horizontally, because the three controls sit side by side and overlapping hit areas would turn a near-miss into the wrong edit. Steps flagged `needsApproval` are labelled and counted in the header, so where the run will pause is known before it starts rather than discovered during it. The running view lives in this component rather than a separate runner because the plan people agreed to is the thing they want to watch; a second surface would make them re-read a list they had already accepted. The switch is derived, not configured: the first step carrying a status past `pending` ends editing, so a caller cannot show edit controls over a plan that is already executing. Progress is counted from finished steps, never an invented percentage, and each step announces itself once as its status changes, tracked against the previous value so a re-render with unchanged statuses stays silent.
meta.motionNotes: Still, as a user-turn surface: nothing moves on its own and nothing shimmers. Removed steps drop to reduced opacity with a strikethrough rather than animating out, so an edit reads as a changed state instead of a disappearance and remains reversible in place. Reordering changes position immediately without a sliding animation — a swap that animates on every press would slow repeated keyboard moves and add motion to what is a precise, deliberate edit. The remaining motion is the shared colour transition on hover and focus at `--pd-duration-instant`, which drops to instant under prefers-reduced-motion. In the running view only the current step moves: its mark pulses on the working colour. A step waiting on the person holds completely still in the waiting colour, which is the turn-taking grammar applied per row instead of per panel. The progress bar animates its width over `--pd-duration-slow` because it tracks a real, discrete change, and under reduced motion the pulse stops while colour and words continue to carry every state.

headingLevel.description: Level of the title heading, so it fits the outline of the page it's placed in. Defaults to 3.

steps.description: The agent's proposed plan, in order.

allowAdd.description: Let the user add their own steps.

runStatus.description:
Shown while the plan runs, beside the progress count — the one thing happening right
now, in the caller's words ("Reading pricing pages").

needsApproval.description: The step has an external effect and will stop for approval when it runs.

note.description: What happened, for a step that's running, waiting, failed or skipped.

events.name: onRun
events.description: Runs the plan as the user left it — reordered, trimmed, or extended.

events.name: onStop
events.description: Shown throughout the run, never hidden behind a hover.

docs: Requires `cn` at `@/lib/utils`. Mark any step with an external effect as `needsApproval` so the user sees where the run will pause before it starts. This component does not execute steps — it hands the agreed plan to `onRun`.
